::: {.section-mark}
[01]{.num}

## What I actually work on
:::

[Most data science writing is about models. Comparatively little is about **the messy, regulated, consequential systems models get deployed into** — where a wrong number becomes a wrong investment, and a regulator will ask you to show your working. That is the part I find interesting, and it is what I write about.]{.lede}

::: {.areas}
::: {.area}
[Asset risk]{.tag}

### Risk on real networks

Turning an asset register into a defensible view of risk — what the data actually supports, where it is thin, and what follows for spend.
:::
::: {.area}
[AI strategy]{.tag}

### AI that survives contact

Setting a direction for AI in an organisation that has to answer to a regulator — less about capability, more about evidence, assurance and sequencing.
:::
::: {.area}
[Decision science]{.tag}

### Decisions, not dashboards

Optimisation and scenario modelling aimed at a decision someone has to make, rather than a chart someone has to look at.
:::
:::

::: {.section-mark}
[02]{.num}

## How I work
:::

[Four habits that run through everything here. They are less about technique than about **making numbers that survive scrutiny**.]{.lede}

::: {.principles}
::: {.principle}
[i]{.num}

### Derive, don't assert

A count should be the output of a rule you can re-run, not a number someone remembers. [Read more →](posts/derive-dont-assert/index.qmd)
:::
::: {.principle}
[ii]{.num}

### Make disagreement legible

Systems will disagree. The job is to show where, why and by how much — not to pick a winner quietly. [Read more →](posts/four-systems-three-taxonomies/index.qmd)
:::
::: {.principle}
[iii]{.num}

### Ask how it could be wrong

Find the assumptions that carry the decision, and test them before anyone else does. [Read more →](posts/what-would-have-to-be-true/index.qmd)
:::
::: {.principle}
[iv]{.num}

### Treat the page as evidence

The reader only has the document. A clipped diagram reads as missing data. [Read more →](posts/presentation-is-evidence/index.qmd)
:::
:::

::: {.pullquote}
A few are probably wrong — but hopefully interesting in the attempt.
:::
